headline: Oregon State–led team unveils water-tolerant MOFs that capture CO2 from humid flue gas
summary: An international team co-led by Oregon State chemist Kyriakos Stylianou reported in Nature a new class of metal-organic frameworks that keep CO2 selectivity in wet flue gas by spatially decoupling CO2 and H2O into separate adsorption sites; a screen of 325,000+ MOFs found two water-stable structures that outperform activated carbon and zeolite 13X from flue-gas to DAC-dilute concentrations.
co2crc_note: Water-tolerant sorbents cut the flue-gas-drying penalty that drives capture cost — directly relevant to CO2CRC/Australian post-combustion and DAC capture R&D and MMV work.
extractor_note: Peer-reviewed primary citation (Nature) confirmed via search; EurekAlert release dated 6 Oct 2026. Direct page fetch blocked by egress proxy this run.

headline: Skytree secures €1m Dutch state development loan for a geothermal-powered DAC Skypark in Iceland
summary: Amsterdam DAC developer Skytree secured a €1 million development loan from Dutch state-backed investor Invest International to fund engineering, permitting and site preparation for a geothermal-powered direct-air-capture Skypark in Iceland, extending its Netherlands Skypark model; captured CO2 is destined for horticulture, food and synthetic fuels, with installation and commercial start targeted for 2028.
co2crc_note: Small early-stage development loan; of interest as a state-backed development-finance template for scaling DAC projects internationally.
extractor_note: Development loan (not a project FID); amount €1m. Dates confirmed via multiple sources (nltimes 2026-10-06, hortidaily, ioplus, gasworld). Direct fetch blocked by egress proxy.

headline: From the Netherlands to Norway: the CO2 journey reshaping European CCS
summary: A Materia Rinnovabile / Renewable Matter analysis of the cross-border CO2 transport-and-storage chain linking Dutch capture projects to Norwegian sub-seabed storage; a feature rather than a discrete announcement.
